messages:
laura: quick triage - since the kernel-selector rollout (yesterday) we're seeing ~8-12% host CPU uplift on inference hosts. pprof flame points to grpc header parsing + request pretokenize hot path. attaching a tiny sample dump below, notably parse_headers -> proto_unwrap -> tokenize()
laura: ```
# sample stack (aggregated)
30.1%  parse_headers
18.2%  proto_unwrap
12.5%  tokenize
7.0%   kvcache_lookup
5.1%   writev (many small writes)
---
calls: increased small write syscalls from 120/s -> 420/s per worker
``` 
laura: this matches the latency tail increases we've seen on 99p and the CPU bump on host-level graphs. any quick ideas before we escalate? @matt @kai
matt: ack, will take a look. do you have a pprof link or raw perf data? also which commit rolled the selector? (need git sha)
l a u r a: (edited) oops pasted wrong formatting, commit is 1a2b3c4 - kernel-selector: use-seqlen-hint for kernel choice. pprof upload: https://internal/prof/6550001110/pprof.html
kai: short read: switching kernels changed default minibatch heuristic (smaller batches for short seqs) which can increase per-request overhead. also writev spike suggests more fragmented writes after tokenization. could be host-side frame assembler now emitting many small frames.
ben: observed kv cache miss rate up ~2x for these workloads after rollout. hypothesis: the kernel picks a variant with slightly different kv key layout/seq alignment causing more cache churn. That could increase proto_unwrap work (more lookups) and tokenization overhead if we re-scan tokens.
laura: @ben can you paste the kv miss numbers? i saw miss ratio go from 0.04 -> 0.09 on p99 hosts
ben: ```
kv_lookup_total: 1,200,000
kv_lookup_miss: 108,000  # 9.0%
previous_miss: 48,000    # 4.0% pre-rollout
``` 
anita: for immediate mitigations: 1) coalesce headers + small payloads into one buffer before parse (reduces tokenize/writev churn), 2) enforce writev aggregation on ingress path, 3) temporarily bias kernel-selector to the older kernel for hosts with >10% writev growth
matt: agree. quick experiment ideas: add an ingress-side coalesce shim (Rust proxy) with a simple buffer threshold (e.g., hold up to 2KB or 5ms) and measure cpu/writev. that should be a low-risk canary.
kai: also add a microbench for header parse with and without coalescing. we should add it to perf-ci to avoid regressions.
laura: i've kicked off a small canary: infra tag hostgroup=hs-grpc-canary, rolled back kernel-selector to 0f9e8d for those nodes. initial telemetry (10 min): CPU down ~6% vs rollout hosts, writev drop ~65% on canary bucket.
laura: can we get an owner for the PRs? two PRs: (A) coalesce shim on ingress proxy, (B) kernel-selector bias fallback + metric gating (auto-revert if writev>300/s)
matt: i'll own PR B (selector bias + gating). will send draft in the next 90 minutes. @anita can you and ben pair on the coalesce shim (PR A)?
anita: yup, ben and I will pair. planning a tiny rust shim under proxy/ingress/coalesce. will keep it feature-flagged.
ben: i'll add an e2e microbench to measure kv miss behaviour when switching kernels. also will add a small histogram for per-request writev count so we can alert on regressions.
laura: thanks. next steps: matt -> draft selector-gate PR, anita+ben -> coalesce shim draft, kai -> add header-parse microbench to perf-ci, laura -> monitor canary and escalate if the revert doesn't hold. I'll create a tracking issue.
sre-bot: created incident INC-2026-042 (host-parse-cpu-uplift), linked to thread 6550001110
matt: thanks. one more ask: can we also add a temporary metric that reports "parse+tokenize CPU pct" so we can quick-alert? if we have that in the dashboards we can roll faster.
laura: good call. i'll add a derived metric (cpu.percent_parse_tokenize) and wire to the host dashboard. will post the dashboard link here once done.
anita: +1. plan to run the coalesce canary behind feature flag for 24h, will report perf deltas before rolling wider.
matt: assigning myself to PR B and reviewing PR A tonight. :thumbsup:
laura: great, adding owners to the tracking issue. thanks all.
